summary: PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19 extracts Česnavičius, Purity for the Brauer group (Duke Math. J. 168 (2019) 1461–1486), read as arXiv v4 and the author's copy. It has 178 items (150 missing, 13 planned, 15 library), 17 routes and five source issues. The library citations hold, and the perfectoid, adic and local-algebra routes still fit their layers after RS-05, RS-08 and RS-02. Four findings. (1, high) The paper's purity programme is routed to SF.0, SF.2 and SF.4, which plan none of it. Meanwhile PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-SCHOLZE-24 routes the same theorems to its new roadmap PurityForFlatCohomology and two Part IIs. There are at least nine item-level overlaps, and that brief expects this paper to route there. (2, medium) E1 is recorded twice, in this file and in the errata file, with conflicting `affects`. (3, medium) scripts/collation.py wrongly takes this paper to have been read from the Duke version, so E1 never reaches the collation worklist. The same function also hides four other papers, and three of my own earlier red-team fixes would hide theirs. (4, low) Route 1 and one planned item point at SF.0, which RS-25 had narrowed to relative Spec/Proj before the review.
checked: Independence: the extraction is by Claude Code cc-442dc5, continuing earlier checkpoints by cc-fb70e5 and cc-7b31c4; its review is by cc-d67081. This worker (Claude Code, cc-c2c06b) did none of them and did not work on PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-SCHOLZE-24.

All 19 stage ids cited by routes or planned items exist in the assembled atlas at 65a02762 (2840 stages, 8007 edges). Routes against the restructurings. RS-25, promoted before the review, narrowed SF.0, SF.1 and SF.4 and kept SF.2: see findings 1 and 4. SF.1 still keeps descent for specified effective classes and algebraic-space quotients, which covers route 2's quotient and representability items. Its torus-H¹ descent items feed the purity argument and could move with finding 1. RS-05, RS-08 and RS-02 were promoted at 20:22 UTC on 23 September, after the review. What routes 7–17 send still fits what P1, P2, P5, P7, A1 and H0 keep (for example, P5 keeps ECD 6.4(o)–(iii) for route 12, and P7 keeps Frobenius-controlled integral towers). The same holds for R03.3, which keeps depth, Auslander–Buchsbaum and complete-intersection criteria (route 5), and for R07.1, which keeps its finite group-scheme classification and imports Cartier duality (route 17). P3, H1:henselian and RG2.0a are kept.

Library citations: all 34. 30 resolve in the pinned declaration index. The other four exist in the source but are missing from the index. Mathlib's IsAdicComplete.henselianRing is an instance, at RingTheory/Henselian.lean:170. Tau Ceti's FiniteLocallyFreeCommAffineGroupSchemeCat.cartierDuality, cartierDual and cartierDualDualIso are at AffineGroupScheme/CartierDuality/FiniteLocallyFree.lean:232, 275 and 320. Statuses: neither library has Picard groups of schemes, Brauer groups of schemes, lci morphisms, Weil restriction or Henselian pairs beyond HenselianRing. Mathlib has IsRegularLocalRing but not factoriality of regular local rings. strict-henselian is rightly planned at Tau Ceti ModularCurves 4D, which owns 'strict henselisation and completion of strict henselisations'.

The paper. I re-fetched arXiv v4, and its hash matches. Theorems 1.1, 1.3 and 6.1 as printed (pp. 1–2, 13) match items global-gm-purity, global-gm-h3, strict-local-purity and global-purity-h0–h3, with the quasi-compactness hypothesis of 6.1. Lemmas 5.1–5.2 match the route 16 items.

Neighbouring extractions. I searched every paper extraction for Brauer, purity, Hartogs, parafactorial, Elkik and Tougeron items. The overlaps with CS24 are finding 1. Elkik approximation is spread over SF.0, SF.4, DD.1, P3/P5 and several Part IIs by at least seven extractions, this one included. That is an area-level question rather than a defect of this extraction, so I record it here only.

Source issues. E2, E3 and E5 are misprints in Gabber–Ramero, and E4 is one in SGA 2. Their locators say so ('Supporting source GR …, not a finding in the main Česnavičius text'), and the review confirmed them. Their bookkeeping is in finding 2. I did not re-verify the mathematics of E1 beyond the printed statement and its two commutative uses (Proposition 2.3 and Corollary 2.4, pp. 4–5).

findings.claim: This extraction and PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-SCHOLZE-24 (CS24) send the same theorems to different owners. So two design jobs would plan Brauer purity and its local inputs. CS24 proposes a new roadmap, PurityForFlatCohomology, for purity, Gabber's conjectures, Brauer purity, local Picard groups and parafactoriality. Its reason says the atlas has 'no Brauer groups of schemes, local Picard groups or SGA 2 purity', and its brief says 'The pending Česnavičius, Purity for the Brauer group extraction should route here too.' This extraction, completed seven hours after CS24's, routes that material instead to SF.0, SF.2 and SF.4. None of those three stages mentions Brauer groups, purity, Picard groups, Hartogs or parafactoriality. Item-for-item: (a) local-pic-lefschetz (route 4) and CS24/133 are the same theorem, SGA 2 XI 3.13(ii): a Noetherian local complete intersection of dimension ≥ 4 has Pic(U) = 0. (b) parafactorial (route 4) = CS24/132. (c) pic-regular (route 1) = the regular case of CS24/134. (d) hartogs (route 1) ≈ CS24/140. (e) purity-dim2 (route 3) = the first clause of CS24/137 (Grothendieck, Brauer III 6.1 b). (f) strict-local-purity and global-gm-purity, this paper's Theorems 1.3 and 1.1 (route 3), are the regular case of CS24/138, which CS24's prerequisites attribute to this paper. (g) global-purity-h0/h1/h2, Theorem 6.1 for tori (route 3), overlap CS24/141, Theorem 7.2.8(a) for groups of multiplicative type. (h) cohom-brauer and affine-brauer-comparison (route 3) = CS24/118–119 (CS24 route 2). (i) residue-tower-exists and perfectoid-tower-exists, Lemmas 5.1–5.2 (route 16, P7), = CS24/037, whose note reads 'Restates Česnavičius, Purity for the Brauer group, Lemmas 5.1 and 5.2' (CS24 route 3). The split reaches further than these two files. SF.2 also collects HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/16 (purity), BRIGHT-NEWTON-23/48 ('Purity for the Brauer group (Česnavičius; Gabber in this case)') and BENOIST-19/10. DESIGN-PurityForFlatCohomology is still pending, so the owner can be settled before anything is designed.

findings.fix: Settle one owner before DESIGN-PurityForFlatCohomology runs. The recommended owner is CS24's roadmap: it names this paper as a source, and SF.0, SF.2 and SF.4 plan none of this. (1) Add a `new` route to PurityForFlatCohomology with CS24's id and title ('Purity for flat cohomology and the conjectures of Gabber'), coalescing as other shared new roadmaps do (ArcTopologyAndDescent, for example). Give it the purity programme: route 3's strict-local and global purity items (purity-dim2 … strict-local-purity, local-torus-h2, the support and coniveau items, global-purity-h0–h3, global-gm-purity, global-gm-h3, the codimension-one intersection, residue and counterexample items), route 1's hartogs and pic-regular, and route 4's parafactorial, local-pic-lefschetz and the SGA 2 IX–XI Picard items. (2) Move cohom-brauer and affine-brauer-comparison into a part-ii route to SchemeAndStackFoundationsFlatCohomologyPartII, coalescing with CS24 route 2. (3) Move residue-tower(-exists), perfectoid-tower(-exists), ramified-unit-root and residue-tower-p-rank into a part-ii route to PerfectoidQuotientsIntegralPerfectoidPartII, coalescing with CS24 route 3; drop route 16. (4) Leave the general foundations where they are: Elkik approximation, Weil restriction, the adic and perfectoid comparison items, and the site/Kummer/fppf prefix. In CS24, update the prerequisite 'not yet extracted' and cite this extraction's items as shared. The alternative is to fold CS24's route 1 into SF.2. That would need a request giving SF.2 a Brauer-purity layer, since SF.2 plans none today; the SF.2 items of HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/16, BRIGHT-NEWTON-23/48 and BENOIST-19/10 would then stay where they are. Under the recommended fix they should import from PurityForFlatCohomology instead.

findings.claim: The nonabelian gap in Proposition 2.2 is recorded twice under the same id, and the two records conflict. This extraction's E1 has affects 'a stated result': its review changed it, and it keeps previousAffects 'the proof'. The errata file's E1 has affects 'the proof', confirmed by its own review (#2271). The corrections differ too: only the errata record offers the weaker, neutral-fibre conclusion as an alternative repair. The locators and printed quotations also differ. The extraction's sourceIssuesRegister says 'E1 is copied unchanged from the existing dedicated errata record', which is not so. The published register data/source-issues.json lists PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19/E1 twice, once with each affects. Since only one record says 'a stated result', whether the paper counts as having a stated-result finding depends on which record a reader or tool happens to use. E2–E4's `known` fields still end 'Awaiting independent review', although REV-PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19 confirmed all of them.
findings.evidence: Extraction E1: affects 'a stated result', previousAffects 'the proof'; correction 'State Proposition 2.2 for commutative G … For noncommutative G, supply the missing step …'. Errata E1: affects 'the proof'; correction '… Alternatively, retain arbitrary affine smooth G but weaken the conclusion to triviality of the fibre over the trivial torsor …'; review 'confirmed … Confirmed as a proof gap in the two ac…'. sourceIssuesRegister.note: 'E1 is copied unchanged from the existing dedicated errata record, without a new verdict. The current collector does not deduplicate matching IDs across files; integration should coalesce these two occurrences of E1.' data/source-issues.json: two entries with id PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19/E1, affects 'a stated result' (file …/papers/PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19.result.json) and 'the proof' (file …/errata/PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19.json). arXiv v4 p. 4: 'Proposition 2.2. For a finite, flat map R → R′ of local rings, an open subscheme V ⊂ Spec R, and an affine, smooth R-group scheme G, if (1) … and (2) …; then the following pullback is injective: H¹_et(V, G) ↪ H¹_et(V_{R′}, G).'
findings.fix: Keep one record. I recommend 'a stated result': Proposition 2.2 is itself a numbered statement whose printed generality (arbitrary affine smooth G) is not established, even though its two uses need only commutative G. Put the errata record's neutral-fibre alternative into the kept correction. Then either delete E1 from one of the two files or give it a new id there as a cross-reference. If the errata file keeps the record with 'a stated result', `scripts/check_errata.py` will require `sourceVersions` in that file: arXiv v4 (SHA-256 a62a12bb…8709) and the author copy (SHA-256 4187331e…97a1). Set E2–E4's `known` to 'new' and drop 'Awaiting independent review'.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19.result.json: top level (no sourceVersions); sourceIssues E1–E3 'searched'; scripts/collation.py provenance()
findings.claim: E1 affects a stated result and was read only against arXiv v4 and the author's copy. The review adds: 'Unpaywall lists only the arXiv copy, so the Duke text could not be collated.' Yet the collation worklist does not list this paper, because scripts/collation.py decides it was read from the published version. With no sourceVersions, provenance() falls back to the free-text notes and returns 'published' when a publisher link and a word like 'read' both occur. Here the publisher link is a Springer link to the metadata of Gabber–Ramero's book, a supporting source, in E2/E3's `searched`. The 'read' words include 'collat' in 'could not be collated'. E1 therefore never reaches the version of record. The same function counts any declared sourceVersions entry of kind 'published' as read, even one that says it was not read. That hides BHARGAVA-25, FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21, KEDLAYA-LIU-15 and STEVENS-08, which have 36 stated findings between them. Three earlier red teams of mine recommend adding exactly such an unread 'published' entry: RT-PAPER-HE-LI-SHI-ETAL-23/1, RT-PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21/2 and RT-PAPER-LIU-WOOD-ZUREICKBROWN-24/4. Applied as written, those fixes would hide their papers in the same way.
findings.evidence: At this revision: collation.provenance(result) == 'published'; collation.stated(result) returns E1; `python3 scripts/collation.py` does not list PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19. provenance(): 'if PUBLISHER.search(notes) and READ_IT.search(notes): return "published"'. PUBLISHER matches 'https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/b10047 — Publisher metadata checked; no accessible erratum located …' in E2/E3. READ_IT = 'read|collat|sha-?256|offprint|published (pdf|text|version)'. For declared readings: 'if "published" in declared: return "published"'. The four papers and their unread entries: BHARGAVA-25 ('PDF not read'), FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21 ('paywalled (SMF), not read'), KEDLAYA-LIU-15 ('Not obtained: the SMF text is paywalled'), STEVENS-08 ('Not read: Springer serves it only to subscribers'). Each has provenance 'published' and is absent from the worklist, with 7, 4, 21 and 4 stated findings.
findings.fix: (1) Here, add 'sourceVersions': [{'kind': 'preprint', 'url': 'https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.06456v4', 'read': '2026-09-23', 'sha256': 'a62a12bbe26595aec89d31d24d46774a1ee3eff73c08da0febf5a2b472118709'}, {'kind': 'author copy', 'url': 'https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~kestutis.cesnavicius/brauer-purity.pdf', 'read': '2026-09-23', 'sha256': '4187331ead5a5246acba1c032a2574ffd6ac9ee6fe1a72bb09d46e2e9f9b97a1'}]. Record that the Duke text was not read in readSections, not as a 'published' entry. With these declared readings the worklist lists the paper. (2) Ask the maintainer to make provenance() skip 'published' entries marked unread, or to require a sha256, and to ignore publisher links that belong to supporting sources. Until then, a red-team fix that suggests an unread 'published' entry should list only the texts actually read. That includes my three fixes named above.
